> K5b plan v1 (PLAN ONLY). Full text: ~/.claude/plans/wash-inbox-1-message-greedy-whisper.md. Planned against redoubt 816ff9760 + K5 1-4 (ce95d19ba), read-only.
> 
> OWNER DECISIONS (recommendations):
> OD1 Trigger = frames' release, not a last-handle count: before any dma_alloc frame can reach the pool (only when its holder process ends), the kernel resets the device(s) that could hold its address. A handle count can't work: handles copy across tables/messages; a mapping outlives its handle (Q144); init keeps a copy for re-grant, so 'last handle' would never fire on a driver crash. Invariant is at least as strong as 173: nothing is pooled unless its device was reset after it last saw the frame.
> OD2 DMA pages cannot be lent/transferred/process_mapped (InvalidArgument); unmap drops only the PTE, frame stays charged and registered until process end; set_flags works. blkd copies already; D3 netd must not lend DMA memory (confirm).
> OD3 Reset set on death = the device each run was allocated through + every DMA device the process ever map_device'd (a per-process bitmask). Residual: two DMA-trusted processes sharing physical addresses.
> OD4 Poll bound 1000 us on the time CSR + 100000-read backstop, non-preemptible; worst case one bound per device in the set, only for a broken device.
> OD5 Quarantined frames force-charged to the grant holder (device object's owner, system at boot), may exceed its limit (as R3 does); when that budget is destroyed the charge moves to the destroyed top's parent so free pages stay backed by frames. Never re-enter the pool.
> OD6 On quarantine: device flagged in a registry keyed by MMIO base (outlives the object), all handles to it swept, map_device/dma_alloc -> NotPermitted until reboot.
> OD7 Test-only kernel feature dma-reset-deaf (fail-safe: forces 'not confirmed' after the real write). No reset-off switch: must-fail proof = one recorded run of the attack case on the pre-K5b (merged K5) kernel.
> 
> 1 TRACKING/PATHS: new kernel/src/dma.rs Registry inside MemoryManager (no new lock): per DMA device slot (max 16; extras lose the DMA flag at boot) base, virtio flag, kernel window va, quarantined, reset_epoch, runs[32] {phys,npages,holder pid,charged BudgetRef,epoch,state}. Frames owned by new sentinel mem::DMA_OWNER (PID 254), so no generic free/move path can touch them. owned_mapping accepts a DMA frame held by pid; unmap drops the PTE only; process_map, legacy lend_memory refuse; release_all pass 1 and check_for_duplicates skip DMA_OWNER. Hook: Process::terminate (services.rs), the one funnel for exit/fault/kill/shutdown, right after release_all_memory_for_process: mm.dma_release(pid). Budget destroy, revocation and K5 deadlines reach it via budget::destroy_subtree -> process::killed -> died -> end_process -> terminate. destroy_device frees no frames. handle_close: nothing. Transfers: no DMA frame can be in flight. Mid-dma_alloc death impossible (single MM critical section; no S-mode traps; K5 preempts only on kernel exit); a failed alloc unwinds straight to the pool (address never disclosed). process_create rollback: debug_assert no runs.
> 
> 2 RESET: dma::boot (kmain, before boot_budgets so tables don't eat root's limit) maps each DMA device's first page into a kernel-only window KERNEL_DMA_REGS + slot*PAGE (new abi constant both widths; rv32 0xff7f_0000 after the PLIC in root 1021, rv64 near KERNEL_PLIC_BASE; MEMORY-LAYOUT row) via map_page_inner PID 1 (no ownership claim), and classifies virtio once: magic 0x74726976 @0x000, version 1|2 @0x004. dma::reset: non-virtio -> false without touching; else volatile write 0 to STATUS @0x70, read back until 0 within OD4. dma_release: compute set S, reset each; all confirmed -> pool runs + uncharge, with assert!(slot.reset_epoch > run.epoch); else quarantine all the process's runs and flag failing devices. Already-unmapped frames wait for the same reset. Dead process's MMIO mapping goes with its page tables; it never runs again.

Event: `12fe1e00e974775676e20b26aba9c6cf` · 2026-09-24T21:11:43Z

> K5b plan v2 (PLAN ONLY): one clean plan in ~/.claude/plans/wash-inbox-1-message-greedy-whisper.md (supersedes v1; OWNER DECISIONS amended). Dispositions of K5b-plan-review under the orchestrator's rulings:
> 
> P1-1 ACCEPTED. New rule: a quarantined slot counts as NOT reset, for ever. If any slot in S is quarantined (already or during this release), every Live run of the dying pid is quarantined, including runs through healthy slots, and nothing is pooled. dma_release records confirmed_now (slots confirmed in THIS call); before pooling each run: assert!(confirmed_now superset of S) and assert!(confirmed_now contains run.slot); this replaces v1's epoch comparison. Model mutation K5bQuarantinedSlotCountsAsReset (pool a co-holder's run after quarantine); gen.rs generates second holders on one device. Boot sub-case in dma-reset-quarantine: D1 and D2 both hold runs on the net device; D1 faults, the first reset fails (dma-reset-deaf now fails only the FIRST attempt per device, so a buggy retry or skip would pool and be caught), D1's frames are quarantined; then D2 is killed and its frames must be quarantined too.
> 
> P2-1 ACCEPTED, narrowed with a reason. Legacy MapMemory returns AccessDenied for any range overlapping a DMA registry slot, whatever the grant (mirrors interrupt_claim). Non-DMA device objects (the console UART that log-server maps by legacy grant in most cases) stay grant-reachable until K6: they hold no DMA addresses, and refusing them would break every log-server case. Widen if you want. Knock-on: virtio-probe (bench-virtio-devices) maps all 8 virtio slots by legacy grant, so it becomes that case's first program and finds the slots through map_device handles (edits tests/programs/src/bin/virtio-probe.rs, tests/bench-virtio-devices.toml). Tested in dma-rules: a legacy MapMemory of a virtio slot under a grant -> AccessDenied.
> 
> P2-2 ACCEPTED, OD5 amended. The quarantine charge stays on the run's own charged budget (already paid within its limit). destroy_marked moves it to the destroyed top's parent before return_carve; the parent gets back the whole carve (>= those pages), so no budget goes over its limit and I5 holds. No charge_over, no grant-holder field. The docs commit records this as a refinement of answer 173's 'charged to the grant holder's budget' wording, and why (I5).
> 
> P2-3 ACCEPTED. The dma_alloc ABI row states that DMA memory and its run are held and charged until the process ends, never reclaimed while it lives, 32 runs per device. Bounded pools: blkd does one dma_alloc(DMA_PAGES) in Device::new at bring-up (servers/blkd/src/kernel.rs:67; DMA_PAGES = 1 + DATA_LEN.div_ceil(PAGE), queue.rs:80), one run. D3 netd: rx and tx regions allocated once by the serving thread before thread_create (D3 plan v2, from D3-plan-review P1-4), two runs.
> 
> P2-4 ACCEPTED. The attack case proves reuse by physical address through the reallocating process's own dma_alloc; if reuse can't be arranged within the bound it prints an inconclusive FAIL, which the case forbids (never a vacuous pass). The pre-K5b must-fail run records observed DMA into the steered address, in commit 3's message. The quarantine case searches exhaustively: a checker takes every page the budget tree can still charge (system itself, plus a child of users with all of users' free pages; R6 makes that the whole free pool), using dma_alloc on the empty virtio slots with halving chunk sizes down to 1 page until out of memory, and asserts no run overlaps any quarantined range; run tables (6 x 32) exhausted first means an inconclusive FAIL. Co-holder sub-case added (P1-1).
> 
> P2-5 ACCEPTED as a platform residual (IO-ARCHITECTURE): non-virtio DMA devices are never reset, so any driver death with one in S quarantines all its runs and flags the device until reboot; such platforms get no driver restart, and their answer is hardware confinement (the FPGA DMA channel). Flagging only run-holding devices was rejected: a mapped device can hold any of the process's addresses.
> 
> P3-1 dma_release considers only Live runs with holder == Some(pid), sets every released run's holder to None, and clears Account::dma_mapped at terminate (also zeroed at process_created); a reused PID never sees old runs.
> P3-2 Residual stated beside OD3: quarantine doesn't unmap a flagged device from live co-holders (Q144).
> P3-3 The poll is part of the teardown it runs in, so it is billed by K5's rule: the dying budget for R10 and deadline destruction, the process's own budget for exit or fault. No separate billing code.
> P3-4 rv64 window at 0xffff_ffff_f400_0000 (+64 KiB, 16 slots) under shared root 511: after the largest possible PLIC (64 MiB) and well below the kernel stacks (top 0xffff_ffff_fff8_0000) and image (0xffff_ffff_ffd0_0000). rv32 at 0xff7f_0000. Boot asserts on both widths: the PLIC ends below the window; no overlap with physmap, PROCESS_AREA, stacks or image; the window's entry is a shared kernel root entry.
> P3-5 The kernel reads magic and version only on DMA-flagged entries, and the loader sets the flag only for DT compatible 'virtio' (loader/src/dt.rs:249), so today it is side-effect-free. Stated residual: a non-virtio DMA platform must add a per-entry virtio mark to Devs rather than rely on that read.
> P3-6 The worst case (|S| x 1 ms, |S| <= 16, non-preemptible, on top of R10's ~21 ms) goes into K5's sched-latency notes in the docs commit.
> 
> Commits unchanged in shape: (1) model: I-DMA invariant + 5 mutations + contracts; (2) kernel: dma.rs, DMA_OWNER, window + asserts, the call changes and legacy refusals, dma_release with the P1-1 rule, quarantine, sweep, charge migration, deaf feature; (3) boot cases, programs, virtio-probe move, knock.rs only if D3's peer hasn't merged, plus the must-fail evidence; (4) docs, including the OD1 reading and the OD5 refinement under answer 173.

> P2-1 ruling folded into the plan file (section 2, Legacy MMIO). The legacy MapMemory refusal is computed on page-rounded bounds, [base & !0xfff, round_up(base + size)), with overflow refused as InvalidArgument. It rejects any partial or whole overlap with a DMA slot's MMIO pages, before anything is claimed or mapped. dma-rules tests two partial overlaps: a range starting one page below a virtio slot and running into it, and an unaligned base inside the slot. Noted: WP-K6 deletes the remaining legacy MapMemory, including the UART grant path.

Event: `37984831a9506f6f13c23f8a11794a5d` · 2026-09-24T21:14:37Z

> K5b plan final edits for the v2 re-review (red: OK with notes), folded in place into ~/.claude/plans/wash-inbox-1-message-greedy-whisper.md. PLAN ONLY.
> - N1 (P2): taken. destroy_marked runs return_carve(top) FIRST, then re-charges quarantined runs from dying budgets to top's parent with a plain charge (it can't fail: q <= the subtree's usage <= top.pages_limit, which was just returned; the charge expects this, citing I5). With no parent the run is uncharged. The model mirrors the order (carve first, then payer migration). New contract: a parent at its limit, whose child quarantined q pages, has that child destroyed; the migration succeeds and the parent ends at or under its limit.
> - P3 a: taken. The legacy MapMemory check rounds the request out to whole pages and compares it, half-open, with the FULL page-rounded MMIO range of every DMA-flagged Devs entry. dma-rules tests: a partial overlap from one page below (refused), an unaligned base inside (refused), and a granted range ending exactly at the slot base, the adjacent UART page (allowed).
> - P3 b: taken. DMA devices beyond 16 get no device object at all; legacy MapMemory is still refused for them, because the check reads every DMA-flagged Devs entry, not the registry.
> - P3 c: taken. The orchestrating program destroys users (it runs nothing in this case), puts every free page of root into a checker budget, and records F (root's and system's free pages via budget_usage). The two then dma_alloc on the empty slots with halving chunks until OutOfMemory. It asserts: pages allocated plus page tables charged == F; no budget has a free page left (by R6 and backed free pages, the whole pool); no run overlaps a quarantined range. Run tables exhausted first = inconclusive FAIL.
